title: Local Rules, Global Efficiency: Emergent Coordination on Large-Scale Road Networks

problem.claim: Individually optimal routing decisions can create system-wide congestion that increases travel time for all participants.

gap.claim: Adaptive city-scale coordination among thousands of decentralized vehicles is still unresolved.

contributions.claim: Autonomous vehicles are presented as an opportunity for dynamic coordination that adapts to traffic conditions.

narrative_sequence.summary: Individually optimal routing can produce system-wide congestion.
Traffic engineers use rigid infrastructure interventions to manage conflicting traffic flows.
Manually designed interventions constrain traffic unnecessarily during off-peak hours because they are optimized for peak demand.
Autonomous vehicles could enable traffic coordination that adapts dynamically to conditions.
City-scale adaptive coordination among thousands of decentralized vehicles remains unresolved.

source_observation.claim: Rigid interventions optimized for peak demand can unnecessarily constrain off-peak traffic.

interpretation.claim: Coordination mechanisms may need to adapt to changing demand rather than enforce fixed operating rules.

application.claim: For dynamic transportation systems, consider adaptive coordination policies that respond to current traffic conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that adaptive coordination is effective at city scale.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proposed coordination method.
The abstract does not report experiments, datasets, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe how decentralized vehicles coordinate at city scale.
